correction.textOverride: Many of the barriers to trade exists not because of a lack of markets or customers, but because there are major barriers to getting products to market at competitive prices. Transaction costs is significant for companies—not only the straight exchange costs, but also the cost of converting, paying, and hedging funds just to pay for the goods and services. Having a common currency mean that many of those transaction costs disappear and the savings can reinvested back into firms’ productivity and innovation. Basically, useless costs turns into productive costs—with longer-term benefits to the whole economy. By unifying some of the currencies, whole economies benefits and grow more than they would as independents. So a common currency provide for a strong economic foundation that all can benefit from.
